summary: As of October 16, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.31 percentage points, +0.20 percentage points over five trading days, and the junk-versus-safe gap is 2.46 percentage points. VIX is 19.99 and the 3-month VIX is 20.50, so near-term fear is below the 3-month reading. The Nasdaq-100 is -6.6 percent from its trailing high, semiconductors are +5.6 percent versus their 200-day average, and 73 percent of the 30-name list is above its own 200-day average.
what_would_change_this: The headline would leave risk-on if junk spreads reached 4.50 percentage points, near-term volatility rose above the 3-month reading by more than half a point, or the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 10 percent below its trailing high.
what_the_tape_is_saying: As of October 16, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.31 percentage points and are up 0.20 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are up 0.02 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 10.94 percentage points. Of the 0.05 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.20 was the credit spread and 0.15 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 5.09 percent as of October 16, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.43 percent as of October 16, 2026, a gap of 0.34 percentage points. Brent is 109.21 dollars a barrel as of October 19, 2026 (+2.40 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.38 percent as of October 19, 2026, up 0.04 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.74 percent as of October 16, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.40 as of October 16, 2026, +2.05 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 18.44 as of October 19, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.76 trillion dollars as of October 14, 2026, up 9 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 3.02 trillion dollars as of October 14, 2026, up 8 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.33 billion dollars as of October 19, 2026, up 0.055 billion over the latest four observations.
